rounds.text: Plastiblends India Ltd trades at a highly attractive P/E of 11.6x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of just 1.04x [E2], representing a steep discount compared to the broader sector benchmark P/E of 21.28x [E6] and sector P/B of 1.84x [E7]. Fundamental momentum is accelerating sharply, highlighted by a 41% surge in trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth [E21], a recent 57% year-on-year net profit expansion [E67], and improving operating margins that stand at 8% in the TTM period compared to 7% three years earlier [E30]. The company is virtually debt-free with a pristine debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x [E38] and declining borrowings down to ₹ 17 Cr [E39], while actively funding future expansion through an 83.3% increase in capital work-in-progress to ₹ 11 Cr [E40]. Furthermore, the business benefits from a robust sector tailwind in chemicals with a tailwind score of +0.73 [E72], backed by a flawless relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E50] and a healthy dividend payout of 24.2% [E60]. conceded: [E14], [E18], [E22], [E34], [E36], [E41].

The valuation is unsupported by intrinsic fundamentals, evidenced by a discounted cash flow model showing intrinsic value at Rs 196 per share against a market price of Rs 205, translating to a negative margin of safety of -4.7% [E44, E45]. Compounded performance reveals severe long-term stagnation, with 10-year sales growth at 4%, 10-year profit growth at -1%, and 10-year share price growth at -1% [E14, E18, E22]. Return metrics persistently languish, exemplified by a 3-year median return on equity of 8% and a recent low ROE of 7.6% [E13, E28]. Cash generation quality is troubling, demonstrated by a cash conversion ratio of 0.57x where profits outpace cash and free cash flow sits at Rs -6 Cr for Mar 2026 [E34, E36]. Furthermore, insider commitment is eroding, as promoter holding declined from 64.38% in Dec 2023 to 62.07% in Sep 2026 [E41], alongside foreign institutional holdings dropping to 0.26% [E42]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x [E38] and trades close to its book value [E2].

Conceded: a DCF model puts intrinsic value at Rs 196 against a market price of Rs 205 [E44, E45], long-term sales and profit growth over 10 years are stagnant or negative [E14, E18], and promoter and foreign institutional holdings have recently decreased [E41, E42]. However, the bear overlooks that TTM profit growth has surged by 41% [E21] and quarterly net profit jumped 57% YoY [E67], showing that historical stagnation is giving way to a powerful operational turnaround that the trailing backward-looking metrics completely miss. Furthermore, the bear's focus on low historical ROE ignores that operating margins have expanded by 1 percentage point both in the TTM period and in the most recent quarter [E30, E31], while capital expenditure is aggressively ramping up with CWIP jumping 83.3% to Rs 11 Cr [E40]. Cash generation concerns are mitigated by a pristine balance sheet featuring near-zero debt with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.03x [E38] and positive operating cash flow of Rs 21 Cr [E35], while the stock trades at an attractive P/E of just 11.6x [E1] and a P/B of 1.04x [E2] that compare favorably to sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. Finally, the bear dismisses the strong technical and fundamental momentum where the relative-strength rating hits a maximum of 100 against the Nifty 500 and the price trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E49, E50].

Conceded: TTM profit growth surged by 41% [E21], quarterly net profit jumped 57% YoY [E67], operating margins expanded by 1 percentage point [E30, E31], CWIP increased by 83.3% to Rs 11 Cr [E40], and the stock holds a relative-strength rating of 100 above its moving averages [E49, E50]. However, this momentum operates against a backdrop of prolonged structural stagnation, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 4% and a 10-year profit growth of -1% [E14, E18]. The bull's reliance on recent margin expansion ignores that the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends both read inconsistent [E32, E33], while long-term returns remain anchored by a depressed 3-year median ROE of 8% [E28]. Furthermore, while operating cash flow reached Rs 21 Cr [E35], it translated into a negative free cash flow of Rs -6 Cr [E36], accompanied by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.57x where profits far outstrip actual cash generation [E34]. Finally, insider confidence is visibly leaking as promoter holdings have declined to 62.07% (-2.31 percentage points) and foreign institutional holdings have dropped to 0.26% [E41, E42].
